policy_cases.name: descriptive_evidence
policy_cases.title: Checkout preference readout
policy_cases.scope: Survey observations from a defined customer cohort.
policy_cases.report_thesis: The survey describes current checkout preferences without attributing an outcome.
source_evidence: Among surveyed customers, 41% selected account checkout as their preferred option.
The survey recorded preferences during a single fieldwork period.

limitations.text: The survey does not establish a cause, forecast, or operating consequence.

expected_policy: do not invent predictions, causality, business impact

policy_cases.name: strongly_actionable_evidence
policy_cases.title: Deployment control recommendation
policy_cases.scope: A report with an explicit source recommendation for a defined rollout decision.
policy_cases.report_thesis: The report directly recommends a pre-deployment control review for the stated rollout.
source_evidence: The report recommends that teams review supplier controls before deploying the new workflow.
The report identifies missing supplier-control evidence as a rollout risk.

candidate_implications.text: A MarketLense recommendation may condition a rollout review on the reported control gap.

expected_policy: add analyst interpretation only when it follows without introducing a new factual premise
recommendations must be explicitly marketlense-authored, conditional and traceable to supplied evidence
classify source-derived factual statements as factual and marketlense-authored recommendations as recommendation

policy_cases.name: insufficient_evidence
policy_cases.title: Partial interview note
policy_cases.scope: A partial observation without a documented sample, comparison, or outcome.
policy_cases.report_thesis: The available evidence is too narrow to establish an implication or recommendation.
source_evidence: One interview participant mentioned interest in a revised service option.
No adoption result, financial impact, operational effect, or forecast was supplied.

limitations.text: The evidence is a single partial observation and does not support extrapolation.

policy_cases.name: recommendation_vs_factual_claim
policy_cases.title: Observed service preference
policy_cases.scope: A source-backed observation with a separately authored conditional recommendation.
policy_cases.report_thesis: The source reports a measured preference; any MarketLense action remains conditional and separate.
source_evidence: The source found that 62% of surveyed customers preferred appointment reminders by text message.

candidate_implications.text: MarketLense recommendation: if the surveyed cohort matches the target audience, test text-message reminders before broader rollout.

limitations.text: The result is limited to the surveyed cohort and does not establish a performance outcome.

expected_policy: classify source-derived factual statements as factual and marketlense-authored recommendations as recommendation; never present a recommendation as a source claim
recommendations must be explicitly marketlense-authored, conditional and traceable to supplied evidence
